web_evidence.title: FROM THE CORNER OF HIS EYE Excerpt
web_evidence.note: The author's site presents a Bantam-authorized excerpt spanning Chapters One through Three. It consistently narrates Barty, Agnes, Joey, Junior, and Naomi externally as he or she while entering several characters' thoughts; its isolated generic you is aphoristic rather than sustained second-person narration.

search_log: Searched "From the Corner of His Eye" Dean Koontz with excerpt, first chapter, point of view, narrator, first person, and third person terms.
Opened the authorized excerpt on Dean Koontz's site; it contains Chapters One through Three and sustained third-person narration across multiple focal characters.
Checked Google Books and Open Library previews; their accessible pages supplied metadata, synopsis, and isolated snippets rather than additional sustained diagnostic prose.

Opened Kirkus book and audiobook reviews; they describe the full novel's intertwined strands, large cast, and performed audiobook narrator but do not explicitly identify grammatical narrative person, so they were not treated as direct person evidence.
Ran targeted searches for epistolary, diary, frame narrative, multiple narrators, and alternating point of view; no credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person sections was found.
An unauthorized free-novel result exposed interior prose but was not used as evidence; the supplied interior Goodreads passages already provide independent corroboration.
person_note: The base narration is third person with shifting focalization among a large cast, not alternating grammatical person. Interior quotes q00060, q00066, q00069, q00077, and q00081 provide sustained external narration and access to characters' perceptions or knowledge; shorter he, she, and named-character quotations remain unmarked rather than being counted mechanically. First-, second-, and plural-person forms in the gnomic and dialogue quotations are universal reflections or character speech. The Bantam-authorized opening independently shows the same third-person method across three chapters and several focal characters. Web coverage is strongest for the opening rather than the entire book, but the diagnostic interior quotations corroborate it and no frame, diary, epistolary structure, or sustained contrary-person section was found.
